data.title: Judge To Rule Quickly On Dismissal Of David Hearn Indictment
data.description: According to CNBC, a Washington judge said Friday he will rule quickly on whether to dismiss with prejudice the now-discredited indictment against former U.S. Olympic canoeist David Hearn over vandalism allegations tied to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. Prosecutors told D.C. Superior Court Judge Todd Edelman they want the case dismissed without prejudice, which would allow them to seek charges again if new evidence emerges, while Hearn's lawyer argued the case should be permanently closed. Prosecutors have said there are no current grounds to sustain a criminal case, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Michael Spence said there is a public interest in allowing a future grand jury to act if new information comes to light. Hearn was indicted in early July on a destruction-of-property charge after U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro said he intentionally damaged a two-square-foot piece of liner from the Reflecting Pool on June 19, but Pirro later moved to dismiss the case after the Interior Department said the damage stemmed from a flawed installation.

data.title: Zelenskyy Says Ukraine Will Not Launch Air Strikes During U.S. Envoys' Visit
data.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine will not launch air strikes during the visit of U.S. President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. According to Sina Finance, Zelenskyy said the two are due to visit Russia in the coming days and Ukraine on September 6, and that Ukraine is preparing for the visits and has held a meeting with its diplomatic team responsible for work with the United States.

He said Ukraine will ensure Russian airspace operates normally during the relevant period so the U.S. negotiators can arrive safely, and that Russia should take reciprocal measures and stop air attacks for the time needed for the talks and related logistics issues. Zelenskyy also said Ukraine hopes the visit and talks with the United States will be as constructive and substantive as possible, and will look for practical ways to help end the war.

data.title: Sudan South Attack Kills 21 Civilians
data.description: According to Sina Finance, a civil group called Sudan Doctors Network said on September 4 that armed attacks hit several areas in South Kordofan State in southern Sudan, killing 21 civilians, including women and children, and injuring several others. The group condemned attacks by the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North on September 3 in multiple parts of Kadugli, South Kordofan State, and said the movement had not responded. The statement said the conflict in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people over more than three years.

data.title: Russia Says Ukraine Distorted Facts Over Airspace Safety Notice
data.description:
Russia's Foreign Ministry said on its website on the 4th that Ukraine's notice about Russian airspace “no longer being safe” distorted the facts and misled users of Russian airspace. According to Sina Finance, the ministry said the Ukrainian remarks posed a direct threat to civil aviation, that Russian authorities were maintaining contact with the International Civil Aviation Organization, and that an urgent appeal had been sent to the ICAO secretary-general.

The ministry said Russia has always firmly safeguarded civil aviation safety. According to Sina Finance, Ukraine said on the 1st that U.S. President Donald Trump warned international airlines in an evening address that Russian airspace was becoming dangerous, while Russian Transport Minister Nikitin said on the 2nd that the transport ministry was continuing to raise flight safety and airport security requirements and that Russia had the ability to respond to all threats.

data.title: AMC Seeks Robinhood Tokenized Stocks Removal Amid Social Media Clash
data.description: AMC wants its tokenized stocks removed from Robinhood, arguing buyers do not own AMC shares and could mistake the products for real equity. According to BeInCrypto, Robinhood Chief Legal Officer Dan Gallagher said the firm will not remove the tokens, while AMC CEO Adam Aron said he will raise the issue with the SEC. The dispute centers on offshore-issued debt instruments tied to stock prices, with no voting rights or right to exchange for the underlying shares.

data.title: BlackSun Raises $1 Billion for Sports and Media Fund
data.description:
BlackSun raised $1 billion for a new sports and media fund, according to Bloomberg.

BlackSun CEO Antonn Muhammed said the private equity firm believes in "compassionate capitalism" and aims to provide services for everyone as well as investors. Former boxing world champion Roy Jones Jr., who leads BlackSun's boxing group Knockout Fights, said the new venture includes physical and financial protections for athletes in a dangerous sport.

data.title: Morgan Stanley Highlights Dividend Stocks as September Trading Turns Volatile
data.description: According to CNBC, Morgan Stanley screened the Russell 1000 for companies that raised dividends by at least 15% quarter over quarter in the past 12 months and highlighted East West Bancorp, Packaging Corporation of America and Devon Energy among its picks. East West Bancorp raised its quarterly dividend by 20 cents to 80 cents a share in January, reported second-quarter earnings of $2.63 per share on revenue of $791 million in July, and lifted its full-year net interest income growth forecast to 7% to 9% from 6% to 8%. Packaging Corporation of America increased its quarterly dividend by 20% in May, bringing the annual payout to $6 a share. Devon Energy, which Morgan Stanley called its favorite exploration and production name in the sector on Friday as oil prices approached $100 a barrel, raised its dividend to 32 cents per share in May. Morgan Stanley strategist Todd Castagno said dividends can provide a steady income stream, signal confidence to the market and help stabilize portfolios during periods of uncertainty and high valuations.
